title: Sabyasachi Opens Lavish 26,000 Sq Ft Delhi Flagship With Met Jewellery Debut
excerpt: India’s biggest luxury fashion store features a Kolkata-inspired design with 120 chandeliers and a Byzantine jewellery collection created with New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art.
body:
• Sabyasachi Mukherjee has opened a 26,000 sq ft flagship store at The Citadel in Mehrauli, New Delhi — more than double the brand’s previous Delhi footprint — featuring a dedicated high jewellery salon.
  • The store is designed as an immersive journey through Kolkata, with 120 chandeliers, 200 antique carpets, 300 original paintings, and a life-size Bengal tiger inside a tramcar-inspired installation.
  • Alongside the store opening, Sabyasachi unveiled a multi-year collaboration with The Metropolitan Museum of Art for a Byzantine-inspired jewellery collection debuting at New York Fashion Week on September 15.
  • About 40% of the brand’s revenue comes from the United States, with a strong following among NRIs, as Sabyasachi expands beyond fashion into jewellery, accessories, and cosmetics.

Designer Sabyasachi Mukherjee has opened his largest retail space to date — a 26,000 sq ft flagship store in Mehrauli, New Delhi — in a bold statement about the future of Indian luxury. The store, which opened on August 25 at The Citadel on One Style Mile, more than doubles the area of the brand’s earlier dual-building location in the same neighborhood.

A Walk Through Kolkata

The new flagship is less a retail space than a museum that happens to sell clothes and jewellery. Its rooms and corridors are arranged as a journey through Kolkata, the city where Sabyasachi launched his label in 1999. One corridor recreates the spirit of Hogg Market, packed with an eclectic collection of objects. Another draws on Chowringhee, the boulevard where the designer’s own office sits. At the store’s heart, a room built to look like a Calcutta tramcar — panelled in wood and etched star-cut glass — houses a life-size sculptural Bengal tiger.

The numbers are staggering: approximately 120 chandeliers, nearly 200 antique carpets, 300 original paintings from the Sabyasachi Art Foundation, and more than 100 antique textiles, mirrors, and decorative objects. Mother-of-pearl inlay, pink Sarrancolin marble, and life-sized statues fill the space alongside embroidery that creeps across walls, panels, cupboards, and ceilings.

"“Even before the New York store opened, 30-35% of our turnover came from America,” Mukherjee told Mint Lounge."

“I have never believed that a luxury store should simply sell products. It should inspire curiosity, preserve culture and create memory. Commerce may bring people through the door, but culture is what makes them return.”
— Sabyasachi Mukherjee

The Met Collaboration

The store opening coincides with one of the most significant partnerships in Indian fashion. Sabyasachi has entered a multi-year collaboration with New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art to create a Byzantine-inspired high jewellery collection, starting at $2,000. It is the Met’s first licensing engagement directed toward the Indian audience, according to Josh Romm, the museum’s head of global licensing and partnerships.

The collection — featuring pieces crafted in 18-karat and 22-karat gold with hand-cut gemstones — will debut on September 15 at Sabyasachi’s New York Fashion Week show, marking his return to the American runway after 20 years. Each piece draws from the Met’s collection of sculptures, coins, pillars, and funerary objects, reinterpreted through Indian craft techniques including Jadau gem-setting, tiger-claw settings, and hand-hammered bezels.

A Global Ambition Rooted in NRI Demand

Sabyasachi’s international push is grounded in real numbers. About 40% of the brand’s revenue already comes from the United States, with strong demand from NRIs. “Even before the New York store opened, 30-35% of our turnover came from America,” Mukherjee told Mint Lounge. The brand now operates seven flagship stores worldwide, including in New York, with jewellery ateliers in Hyderabad and Dubai.

For Indian Americans planning weddings, festivals, or formal events, Sabyasachi has long been a destination label. The Met collaboration and NYFW return are designed to push the brand beyond the South Asian diaspora and into the broader American luxury market.

Beyond Fashion

Mukherjee — who called himself a “businessman” five times during a recent interview and not once a designer — is building Sabyasachi into a diversified luxury house. The brand is expanding into sunglasses, footwear, leather goods, and cosmetics, with its accessories business expected to cross ₹100 crore this year. The jewellery line, which includes the Met collection, is central to a strategy that prizes craft over trends.

“Craftsmen are not transactional people,” Mukherjee said. “If craft skips a generation, it never comes back.”

What’s Next

The Byzantine jewellery collection will debut at NYFW on September 15, followed by wider retail availability. Sabyasachi has also announced plans for gold jewellery and more accessible price points across categories. For now, the Delhi flagship — part gallery, part Kolkata nostalgia trip, part luxury bazaar — is the clearest expression yet of where the brand is headed.
